grammar.title: Written–spoken word pairs
grammar.pattern: 没有 → 未 · 就是 → 即 · 需要 → 需 · 而且 → 且 · 和 → 及
grammar.explain: Formal written Chinese prefers short literary words where speech uses everyday two-syllable ones. 未 replaces 没(有), 即 means 就是, 需 means 需要, 且 means 而且, and 及 joins nouns like 和. Use them in notices, reports and emails; in casual conversation they sound stiff.

grammar.title: The reason why … is that …
grammar.pattern: A 之所以 B，是因为 C
grammar.explain: This formal frame states a result first and then gives the reason: "The reason A does B is that C." The subject comes before 之所以. It is typical of essays, speeches and analysis; in conversation people usually just say "……，是因为……" or "……，主要是因为……".

examples.en: The reason he won is that he stayed calm throughout the second half.
The reason this film moves people is that it tells the story of ordinary people.

grammar.title: Restating: 也就是说 / 换句话说 / 说白了
grammar.pattern: Statement，也就是说 / 换句话说 / 说白了，restatement
grammar.explain: These markers introduce a rephrasing. 也就是说 ("that is to say") spells out a consequence or conclusion; 换句话说 ("in other words") rephrases neutrally; 说白了 ("to put it bluntly") is colloquial and strips away the polite wording.

reading.title: 同一件事，两种说法
reading.zh: 上周，我们小区的业主委员会在大门口贴了一张通知：“因管道维修，本周六上午八时至十二时停水，请各位业主提前做好储水准备。如有疑问，请拨打物业服务电话。”短短几行字，没有一句多余的话。当天晚上，业主群里就热闹起来了。“哎，周六停水啊？那我要早点起来洗澡。”“蛮好的，正好有理由不做饭，出去吃烤串！”“别扯了，你哪天做过饭？”大家你一言我一语，聊得不亦乐乎。仔细想想，这两段话说的是同一件事，风格却完全不同。通知用的是书面语，讲究简洁、准确、得体，“即”“未”“需”“及”这类字随处可见；群聊用的是口语，句子短，语气词多，还夹着玩笑。前者面向所有业主，必须把时间、原因及注意事项一一交代清楚；后者是熟人之间的闲聊，重要的不只是信息，还有人情味。之所以会有这样的差别，是因为说话的场合和对象不同。也就是说，语言本身并没有高低之分，唯有用对了地方，才算用得好。如果在朋友群里说“请各位做好储水准备”，大家多半会以为你在开玩笑；反过来，要是物业的通知写成“哎，周六没水啊”，恐怕业主们也会对它的专业程度有所怀疑。学中文到了这个阶段，与其一味地背单词，不如多留意身边的人在什么场合、用什么方式说话。
reading.en: Last week, the homeowners' committee of our residential compound put up a notice at the main gate: "Due to pipe maintenance, the water supply will be cut off this Saturday from 8 a.m. to 12 noon. All residents are asked to store water in advance. For any questions, please call the property management service line." Just a few short lines, without a single superfluous word. That evening, the residents' group chat came alive. "Hey, no water on Saturday? Then I'll have to get up early to shower." "Great—a perfect excuse not to cook. Let's go out for kebabs!" "Oh, come off it—when have you ever cooked?" Everyone chimed in, chatting away happily. If you think about it, the two passages are about the same thing, yet their styles are completely different. The notice uses written language, which values brevity, precision and propriety, and words like 即, 未, 需 and 及 are everywhere. The group chat uses spoken language: short sentences, plenty of modal particles, and jokes mixed in. The former addresses every resident and must spell out the time, the reason and the points to note one by one; the latter is small talk among people who know each other, where what matters is not only the information but also the human warmth. The reason for the difference is that the occasion and the audience are different. In other words, language itself is neither high nor low; it is only good when it is used in the right place. If you wrote "All residents are asked to store water in advance" in a chat with friends, they would probably think you were joking. Conversely, if the management's notice read "Hey, no water on Saturday", the residents might well have some doubts about how professional it is. At this stage of learning Chinese, rather than simply memorising vocabulary, it pays to notice how the people around you speak, and on what occasions.

grammar.title: Citing sources in the news
grammar.pattern: 据 + source + 报道/介绍，…… · source + 表示 / 称 / 声称 + clause
grammar.explain: News Chinese always names its source. 据……报道 / 据……介绍 ("according to …") opens a sentence. Reporting verbs differ in tone: 表示 is neutral ("said"), 称 is a brief written "stated", and 声称 ("claimed") hints that the claim has not been verified. 对此 ("in response to this") introduces someone's reaction.

examples.en: According to local media, nobody was hurt in the accident.

grammar.title: Linking facts: 与此同时 / 此外
grammar.pattern: Fact 1。与此同时，Fact 2。此外，Fact 3。
grammar.explain: 与此同时 ("at the same time; meanwhile") presents a parallel development, and 此外 ("in addition") adds a further point. Both open a new sentence or clause. They are typical of writing and broadcasts; in conversation people tend to say 同时 or 还有.

examples.en: The new regulations take effect next month. At the same time, the authorities will tighten supervision.

grammar.title: Written particles 将 / 已 / 于
grammar.pattern: 将 + V (will) · 已 + V (already) · V + 于 + time/place
grammar.explain: Headlines and reports favour one-syllable literary words: 将 for the future "will" (spoken 要/会), 已 for "already" (spoken 已经), and 于 for "at / in / on" with a time or place (spoken 在). 于 often comes straight after the verb, as in 位于, 生于, 成立于.

reading.title: 退役球星拍卖勋章，助少女重获新生
reading.zh: 【本报讯】昨晚，一场特别的慈善拍卖会在市体育馆举行。退役足球运动员李强拿出了自己职业生涯中最珍贵的一枚勋章进行拍卖，所得款项将全部用于资助一名急需进行肾移植手术的十二岁少女。李强是本市足球史上的传奇人物，十八岁首次上场，三十岁因腿部骨折告别赛场。这枚勋章多年来一直被他低调地收藏在家中，很少示人。“说实话，有点舍不得，”他在接受采访时表示，“但跟拯救一条生命相比，一枚勋章又算得了什么？”据主办方介绍，当晚共有三百多名民众聚集在体育馆内，不少球迷自发组成啦啦队，为拍卖会加油助威。经过二十多轮竞价，勋章最终以八十六万元成交，买家是一位不愿透露姓名的企业家。令人意外的是，他在拍下勋章后当场宣布，将把它送还给李强本人。现场顿时响起了热烈的掌声。与此同时，市慈善总会已介入此事，负责监管善款的使用，并承诺定期向社会公布明细。医院方面告知记者，女孩的手术预计于下月初进行，目前各项准备工作正在有序展开。也有网友质疑此类活动有作秀之嫌。对此，主办方回应称，所有款项均通过正规渠道转账，欢迎社会各界监督。
reading.en: [Our correspondent reports] Last night a special charity auction was held at the city stadium. Retired footballer Li Qiang put up for auction the most precious medal of his professional career, and all the proceeds will go towards a twelve-year-old girl who urgently needs a kidney transplant. Li Qiang is a legend in the city's football history: he first took the field at eighteen and left the game at thirty after breaking his leg. For many years he had kept the medal quietly at home and rarely showed it to anyone. "To be honest, I find it a bit hard to part with," he said in an interview, "but compared with saving a life, what's a medal?" According to the organisers, more than three hundred members of the public gathered in the stadium that evening, and many fans spontaneously formed cheering squads to support the auction. After more than twenty rounds of bidding, the medal finally sold for 860,000 yuan to an entrepreneur who did not wish to be named. To everyone's surprise, right after winning the medal he announced on the spot that he would give it back to Li Qiang. The venue immediately erupted into warm applause. Meanwhile, the city charity federation has stepped in and will oversee how the donations are used, promising to publish a detailed account at regular intervals. The hospital told reporters that the girl's operation is expected to take place early next month and that all preparations are under way in an orderly manner. Some netizens questioned whether such events are just for show. In response, the organisers said that all funds are transferred through official channels and that they welcome scrutiny from all sectors of society.

grammar.title: 毫不 + two-syllable word

grammar.explain: 毫不 means "not in the slightest". It is followed by a two-syllable verb or adjective and is more emphatic and more written than 一点儿也不. 毫不夸张地说 ("it's no exaggeration to say") is a favourite opener in reviews and online posts.

grammar.title: 凡是……都…… (every … without exception)
grammar.pattern: 凡(是) + description，都 / 一律 + predicate
grammar.explain: 凡 / 凡是 ("every; all who") makes a sweeping statement that covers every case of a kind. The main clause usually contains 都 or the formal 一律 ("without exception"). 凡 on its own is more written; 凡是 is used in speech and writing.

grammar.title: Turning to the other side: 话说回来

grammar.explain: 话说回来 ("that said; then again") turns from one side of an argument to the other, often after a complaint or a joke. It is conversational and very common in online writing, vlogs and reviews; 不过话说回来 is an especially frequent combination.

reading.title: 算法比你更懂你？
reading.zh: 你有没有发现，刚在网上搜过一次露营帐篷，接下来一周，购物网站、短视频平台甚至新闻软件都会不停地给你推荐帐篷？这并不是巧合。如今，我们的每一次点击、每一次停留都会被记录下来，存进服务器上的数据库。平台根据这些数据追踪你的兴趣，模拟你的喜好，再精准地锁定你最可能点开的内容。这种推荐方式确实方便。毫不夸张地说，算法有时比你自己还懂你的心思。然而，它也带来了一个潜在的问题：你看到的东西越来越像，接触到的观点越来越单一。时间一长，人就像被关进了一个由信息织成的茧，这就是所谓的“信息茧房”效应。在茧房里，人们很容易只听得进和自己一致的声音，对不同意见则一味吐槽，甚至恶语相向，理性讨论的空间越来越小。多年来，不少学者一直在研究如何打破这种局面，但至今尚未找到完美的办法。有人建议在推荐中加入一定比例的随机内容，让用户偶尔见识一下圈子以外的世界；也有人认为，归根结底还是要靠每个人自己：多看几种不同来源的信息，遇到情绪化的帖子先别急着转发，守住独立思考的底线。技术的进程不会停下，算法也不可能被完全取代。但愿我们在享受便利的同时，不要把判断的权利也一并交了出去。
reading.en: Have you noticed that after searching for a camping tent online just once, for the next week shopping sites, short-video platforms and even news apps keep recommending tents to you? This is no coincidence. Nowadays every click and every pause we make is recorded and stored in a database on a server. Based on these data, platforms track your interests, simulate your preferences, and then precisely target the content you are most likely to open. This kind of recommendation is certainly convenient. It is no exaggeration to say that algorithms sometimes understand what is on your mind better than you do. However, it also brings a potential problem: the things you see become more and more alike, and the views you encounter become narrower and narrower. Over time, it is as if you have been shut inside a cocoon woven out of information—this is the so-called "information cocoon" effect. Inside the cocoon, people easily listen only to voices that agree with them, while they mock or even abuse differing opinions, and the room for rational discussion keeps shrinking. For many years, scholars have been studying how to break out of this situation, but so far no perfect solution has been found. Some suggest adding a certain proportion of random content to recommendations, so that users occasionally get a glimpse of the world beyond their own circle; others believe that in the end it comes down to each individual: read information from several different sources, hold off on sharing emotional posts, and keep to the baseline of independent thinking. Technological progress will not stop, and algorithms cannot be done away with entirely. Let us hope that while enjoying the convenience, we do not hand over our right to judge for ourselves as well.

grammar.title: Classical function words in modern prose
grammar.pattern: 乃 = 是 · 故 = 所以 / 原来的 · 其 = 他(的) · 之 = 的 · 及其 = 和他(它)的
grammar.explain: Modern written Chinese keeps many function words from Classical Chinese. 乃 means 是 ("to be"), 故 means 所以 ("therefore") or "former" (故乡, 故人), 其 means "his / her / its / their", 之 often replaces 的, and 及其 means "and its / their". They make writing compact and elevated, and appear in essays, literature, slogans and formal notices.

examples.en: Failure is the mother of success.
It is like spring here all year round, hence the name "City of Spring".

grammar.title: Whenever …: 每当……，总(会)……
grammar.pattern: 每当 + situation，(subject) 总(会) / 就 + habitual reaction
grammar.explain: 每当 ("whenever; every time") introduces a recurring situation, and the main clause—usually with 总 or 就—describes what always happens then. It is a favourite of narrative and lyrical writing, especially when recalling memories.

examples.en: Whenever I hear this song, I think of my university days.
Whenever the night grows still, he thinks of his family far away.

grammar.title: Endless feelings: ……不已
grammar.pattern: two-syllable emotion word + 不已 (感动不已 · 后悔不已 · 激动不已)
grammar.explain: 不已 ("without end") follows a two-syllable emotion word to say that the feeling went on and on. It is literary and appears in stories, news features and speeches; in conversation you would say 特别感动 or 一直很后悔.

examples.en: When they heard his story, everyone was deeply moved.

reading.zh: 外婆的老屋在江南的一个小镇上，青砖黑瓦，屋后有一条小河。每当夏天的傍晚，外婆总会搬一把竹椅坐在门口，一边摇着扇子，一边给我讲那些我听过无数遍的故事。她常常慢悠悠地说道：“做人乃是一辈子的事，急不得。”那时我年纪小，只觉得这话像是从古书里搬出来的，并不明白其中的意思。后来我去北方读书、工作，一年难得回去一次。每次临行辞别，外婆总要往我的行李里塞满她亲手做的点心，嘴里念叨着：“外面的东西再好，也不如家里的。”我嫌她啰嗦，却也不忍心拒绝。前年冬天，外婆病倒了。我匆匆赶回去，她已经瘦得让人认不出来，靠在床头，用力握着我的手，半天才说出一句：“回来了就好，回来了就好。”那一刻，我心里难过不已，却硬是忍着没有哭出声来。外婆走后，老屋被卖掉了。去年我顺着那条熟悉的小路再去看它，屋顶换了新瓦，门口的竹椅也不见了，只有河水依旧静静地流着。故人已去，物是人非，可脑海中那个温馨的画面，却永不褪色。我想，人的一生会遗忘很多事情，但有些人、有些话，是怎么也忘不掉的。所谓故乡，大概就是这些记忆及其背后那份说不清的牵挂吧。
reading.en: My grandmother's old house stood in a small town south of the Yangtze, with grey bricks and black tiles and a little river behind it. On summer evenings she would always carry a bamboo chair out to sit by the door and, fanning herself, tell me stories I had heard countless times. She often said, in her unhurried way, "Learning to live well is the work of a lifetime—you can't rush it." I was little then, and the saying sounded to me as if it had been lifted from some ancient book; I didn't understand what it meant. Later I went north to study and work, and could seldom go back more than once a year. Every time I said goodbye before setting off, Grandma would stuff my luggage with snacks she had made with her own hands, muttering, "However good things are out there, they're never as good as home." I found her fussing tiresome, yet I could never bring myself to refuse. The winter before last, Grandma fell ill. I hurried back; she had grown so thin I barely recognised her. Propped up against the head of the bed, she gripped my hand hard, and after a long while managed only, "You're back, that's all that matters, you're back." At that moment I was overcome with grief, yet I forced myself not to cry out loud. After she passed away, the old house was sold. Last year I followed that familiar path to see it again. The roof had new tiles and the bamboo chair by the door was gone; only the river still flowed quietly on. The person I loved was gone; the place remained but nothing was the same. Yet the warm picture in my mind will never fade. I think that in a lifetime we forget a great many things, but some people and some words can never be forgotten. Perhaps what we call home is simply these memories and the inexpressible attachment behind them.

grammar.title: Two-part sayings (歇后语)
grammar.pattern: picture part —— meaning part (often a pun)
grammar.explain: A 歇后语 is a two-part saying: the first half paints a funny or vivid picture, and the second half gives the real meaning, very often through a pun. Speakers frequently say only the first half and let the listener supply the rest, which is part of the fun.

examples.en: A nephew carrying a lantern—lighting his uncle (jiù), i.e. "as before" (zhàojiù).

Fetching water with a bamboo basket—all for nothing.

grammar.title: Homophone puns (谐音)
grammar.pattern: X 和 Y 谐音 → lucky or unlucky meaning
grammar.explain: Chinese has a great many homophones, and puns built on them (谐音) shape customs as well as jokes. 鱼 (yú) sounds like 余 "surplus", so fish is eaten at New Year; 送钟 "giving a clock" sounds like 送终 "attending a deathbed", so clocks are avoided as gifts. Modern internet puns, called 谐音梗, work the same way.

examples.en: People eat fish at New Year because 鱼 "fish" sounds like 余 "surplus".
Never give a clock as a present, because 送钟 sounds like 送终, "seeing someone off at death".

grammar.title: Ironic praise (反话)
grammar.pattern: 你可真行！· 真有你的！· 可真够 + Adj + 的
grammar.explain: Chinese humour often uses 反话, saying the opposite of what you mean. 你可真行！and 真有你的！can be sincere praise, but with a dry tone they mean "Well done—not!". 可真够……的 ("really quite …") adds a sarcastic edge to an adjective. Context and tone tell the listener which meaning you intend.

examples.en: Well done you—you've locked your keys in the house again.
Lovely and "cool" today, isn't it—forty degrees!
You're amazing—you even solved a problem this hard!

reading.title: 谐音梗，扣钱！
reading.zh: 最近，我们公司流行一句话：“谐音梗，扣钱！”这事儿得从我们的上司老张说起。老张为人宽容，平时很少发脾气，唯独受不了下属讲谐音梗。有一次开会，一个刚毕业的小丫头汇报新产品的销量，说产品“卖得像蜂蜜一样，甜到了客户心里”，老张听了还挺满意。谁知她又补了一句：“这就是我们的‘蜜’密武器。”会议室里先是一愣，接着笑成一片。老张哭笑不得，当场宣布：“以后谁再讲谐音梗，扣钱！”其实，中国人玩谐音的历史极为悠久。过年吃鱼，是盼着“年年有余”；结婚时在被子里放红枣和花生，取的是“早生贵子”的意思；元宵节猜灯谜，更是把文字游戏玩出了各种花样。民间还有大量歇后语，比如“外甥打灯笼——照旧（舅）”，意思是一切跟原来一样；“孔夫子搬家——净是书（输）”，用来笑话老是输的人。这些说法大多出自普通人的日常生活，听起来与众不同，却一点儿也不难懂。回想起来，老张的“禁令”并没有坚持多久。一个月后的公司年会上，他自己刚开场就来了一句：“今年大家辛苦了，年终奖保证让大家‘薪’满意足！”台下哄堂大笑，有人大喊：“谐音梗，扣钱！”老张摆摆手：“今天不扣，今天加！”看来，谐音梗就算会扣钱，也迟早会回来的。
reading.en: Lately there's been a popular saying at our company: "Puns cost you money!" It all started with our boss, Lao Zhang. Lao Zhang is easy-going and rarely loses his temper, but the one thing he can't stand is his staff making puns. Once, at a meeting, a young woman fresh out of university was reporting on sales of a new product. She said the product was "selling like honey, sweet right to the customers' hearts", and Lao Zhang seemed quite pleased. But then she added, "This is our honey—sorry, secret—weapon." (蜜 "honey" and 秘 "secret" are both pronounced mì.) The meeting room fell silent for a second and then burst into laughter. Lao Zhang didn't know whether to laugh or cry, and announced on the spot: "From now on, anyone who makes a pun gets docked pay!" In fact, the Chinese have been playing with homophones for a very long time. People eat fish at New Year hoping for "surplus year after year" (余, yú, sounds like 鱼, fish). At weddings, red dates and peanuts are put in the quilt, standing for "may you soon have a son" (早生贵子 sounds like 枣、生、桂子). Guessing lantern riddles at the Lantern Festival turns word games into all sorts of tricks. There are also countless two-part sayings, such as "A nephew carrying a lantern—lighting his uncle (舅, jiù)", meaning everything is "as before" (照旧, zhàojiù), or "Confucius moving house—nothing but books (书, shū)", used to tease someone who always loses (输, shū). Most of these sayings come from ordinary people's daily lives; they sound unusual, yet they are not at all hard to understand. Looking back, Lao Zhang's "ban" didn't last long. At the company's annual party a month later, he opened with: "Everyone has worked hard this year—your year-end bonus is guaranteed to leave you salary-fied!" (薪 "salary" sounds like 心 in 心满意足, "fully satisfied".) The audience roared with laughter, and someone shouted, "Puns cost you money!" Lao Zhang waved his hand: "No docking today—today it's a raise!" It seems that even if puns cost you money, sooner or later they always come back.

grammar.title: Softening requests
grammar.pattern: 你介意……吗？ · 能不能麻烦你……？ · ……，好吗？
grammar.explain: Chinese politeness relies heavily on softeners. 你介意……吗 ("do you mind …?") and 能不能麻烦你…… ("could I trouble you to …?") turn a request into a question, and a tag such as 好吗 or 行吗 at the end invites agreement. Adding 一下 or doubling the verb (看看, 帮帮) also makes a request sound lighter.

grammar.title: Let alone …: 别说……，(就)连……也/都……

grammar.explain: 别说 ("let alone; never mind") sets up the more extreme case A, and 连 B 也 / 都 states that even the easier case B is (or is not) true. The pattern is emphatic and very common in speech.

grammar.title: Saying no without saying 不
grammar.pattern: 恐怕…… · 改天吧 · 我再考虑考虑 · 不太方便
grammar.explain: A blunt 不 can sound cold, so refusals are usually cushioned. Common strategies are giving a reason with 恐怕 ("I'm afraid"), postponing with 改天吧 ("another day"), saying 我再考虑考虑 ("let me think it over"), or using 不太方便 ("not very convenient"). Listeners understand all of these as a polite no.

reading.title: 该不该复合？
reading.zh: 【读者来信】我和男朋友在一起三年，上个月因为一件小事吵了一架，他一气之下提出分手。这几周他又不停地给我发消息，说想复合。朋友们都劝我别心软，还说他早就和别人有来往了，可这只是传闻，我也不知道该不该信。我的直觉告诉我他是真心的，但一想到吵架时他那副失控的样子，我又有点害怕。我该怎么办？【专栏回复】你好！首先，分手后想复合并不少见，关键在于两个人分开的原因有没有真正解决。吵架本身并不可怕，可怕的是每次争吵都在重复同样的问题。你提到他吵架时会失控，这一点值得认真对待：情绪需要发泄，但发泄不能以伤害对方为代价。其次，不要被别人的说法左右。传闻属实与否，你可以直接问他，而不是在心里反复猜测。除此之外，也要问问自己：你想回到这段关系，是因为还爱他，还是只是害怕孤单？如果是后者，那么即使复合，问题迟早还会出现。好的感情需要默契，更需要沟通。不妨约他找个安静的地方，把彼此介意的事情都摊开来谈一谈。如果他愿意为改变付出努力，你们或许可以再试一次；如果他只是想用甜言蜜语把过去的矛盾一笔带过，那就要慎重了。最后想说的是，无论你做出什么选择，都别丢掉自己。真正的爱，不应该让人感到窒息。
reading.en: [Reader's letter] My boyfriend and I have been together for three years. Last month we had a row over something trivial, and in a fit of anger he said we should break up. For the past few weeks he has been messaging me non-stop, saying he wants to get back together. My friends all tell me not to go soft, and say he has been seeing someone else for a long time—but that's only a rumour, and I don't know whether to believe it. My gut tells me he is sincere, but when I think of how he loses control when we argue, I feel a little scared. What should I do? [Columnist's reply] Hello! First of all, wanting to get back together after a break-up is not unusual. The key is whether the reasons you split up have really been resolved. Arguing in itself is not frightening; what is frightening is when every quarrel goes over the same problem again. You mention that he loses control when you argue, and this deserves to be taken seriously: emotions need an outlet, but letting them out must not come at the cost of hurting the other person. Second, don't let other people's opinions sway you. Whether or not the rumour is true, you can ask him directly instead of guessing over and over in your head. Beyond that, ask yourself whether you want to go back to this relationship because you still love him, or simply because you are afraid of being alone. If it is the latter, then even if you get back together, the problems will reappear sooner or later. A good relationship needs mutual understanding, and even more it needs communication. Why not suggest meeting somewhere quiet and talking openly about everything that bothers each of you? If he is willing to make an effort to change, perhaps you can give it another try; if he just wants to gloss over past conflicts with sweet talk, you should be careful. Finally, whatever you decide, don't lose yourself. Real love should never make you feel suffocated.

reading.title: 一封邮件的学问
reading.zh: 小李是公司新来的职员。上周一，他一大早就收到客户的邮件：对方有一批订单急需在月底前交货，希望我们设法提前安排生产。小李想都没想，立刻回复：“没问题，包在我身上！”王经理看到后，把他叫进了办公室。“客户的要求我们当然要重视，但话不能说得太满。”王经理说，“工厂这个月的生产计划早就排满了，万一做不到，客户会觉得我们说话不算数。比较明智的做法是先查明情况，再给对方一个确切的答复。”接着，他教小李重新写了一封邮件：“张总您好！贵公司的需求我们已经收到，目前正在与工厂协调生产进度，预计明天下午给您答复。如有不便，还望谅解。”小李读了两遍，发现这封邮件既没有把话说死，又让对方感受到了诚意。后来，双方安排了一次会面。客户一开始态度比较强硬，坚持要求提前交货，双方差点发生争执。王经理没有跟对方正面冲突，而是拿出一份详细的清单，逐条说明哪些可以提前、哪些确实做不到，并私下提出给予一定的折扣作为补偿。凭借这份坦诚和专业，客户最终同意分两批交货。回公司的路上，小李庆幸地说：“幸亏我原来那封邮件没发出去。”王经理笑了笑：“在这个圈子里，信用比什么都重要。员工手册里那些写邮件的规范，你回去好好看看，会受益一辈子的。”
reading.en: Xiao Li was a new member of staff at the company. Last Monday, first thing in the morning, he received an email from a client: they had a batch of orders that urgently needed to be delivered before the end of the month, and they hoped we could find a way to schedule production earlier. Without a second thought, Xiao Li replied at once: "No problem, leave it to me!" When Manager Wang saw this, he called him into his office. "Of course we must take the client's request seriously, but we can't promise too much," he said. "The factory's production schedule for this month has long been full. If we can't deliver, the client will think we don't keep our word. The wiser approach is to find out the facts first and then give them a definite answer." He then showed Xiao Li how to rewrite the email: "Dear Mr Zhang, we have received your company's request and are currently coordinating the production schedule with the factory. We expect to give you an answer tomorrow afternoon. We apologise for any inconvenience and hope for your understanding." Xiao Li read it twice and realised that the email made no rash promises, yet still conveyed sincerity. Later, the two sides arranged a meeting. At first the client took a hard line, insisting on early delivery, and the two sides almost came to an argument. Manager Wang avoided a head-on clash. Instead he produced a detailed list, explaining point by point what could be brought forward and what really could not, and privately offered a discount as compensation. Thanks to this candour and professionalism, the client finally agreed to delivery in two batches. On the way back to the office, Xiao Li said with relief, "Thank goodness my original email never went out." Manager Wang smiled: "In this business, credibility matters more than anything. Go and read the email guidelines in the staff handbook properly—they'll serve you for the rest of your life."

grammar.title: Admittedly …, but …: 诚然……，但……
grammar.pattern: 诚然，concession，但(是) / 然而 + main argument
grammar.explain: 诚然 ("admittedly; it is true that") concedes a point to the other side before you turn the argument with 但 or 然而. It is a hallmark of debates and argumentative essays; in conversation you might say 确实……，不过…….

grammar.title: So much so that: 以至于
grammar.pattern: situation，以至于 + striking result
grammar.explain: 以至于 ("so much so that; to the point that") links a situation to a striking or extreme consequence. It is more formal than 结果 or 弄得 and is common in arguments and narratives.

grammar.title: In the final analysis: 归根结底 / 说到底
grammar.pattern: 归根结底 / 说到底，+ root cause or key point
grammar.explain: 归根结底 ("in the final analysis; at root") sums up an argument by naming the fundamental cause or point, usually at the start of the concluding sentence. 说到底 is the more colloquial equivalent, and 从根本上说 is more formal.

reading.zh: 正方一辩：谢谢主席。各位评委、各位同学，大家好！我方认为，知识付费利大于弊。在信息爆炸的今天，网上的免费内容多得前所未有，可真正有价值的并不多。我们花大量时间搜寻、搜集资料，最后得到的往往是一堆质量低下的帖子。付费课程则不同：作者有责任把内容讲清楚，读者也会因为付了钱而更加认真。诚然，付费内容并非完美，但它让优质知识的源头得到了应有的回报，这对整个行业的发展至关重要。反方一辩：谢谢主席。对方辩友把付费说成了万能钥匙，我方不敢苟同。首先，花了钱不等于学到了东西。很多人买课只是为了获得一种“我在进步”的虚拟满足感，从头到尾全程听完的人少之又少。其次，不少平台刻意制造焦虑，宣传“不学就会被淘汰”，迫使人们不停地掏钱。在这种氛围之下，买课甚至成了一种炫耀，以至于学习本身反而被忽视了。我们不能低估商业营销对公众认知的影响。正方二辩：对方辩友说有人买了不听，可这是个人的过错，不是知识付费本身的问题。难道因为有人办了健身卡不去，就能说健身房有害吗？反方二辩：我方并非反对付费，而是想提醒大家：归根结底，学习靠的是自己。没有必要非得花钱才能学习，图书馆、免费的公开课同样能让人获益。主席：感谢双方的精彩发言，下面进入自由辩论环节。
reading.en: First speaker for the affirmative: Thank you, Chair. Judges, fellow students, good afternoon! Our side believes that paying for knowledge does more good than harm. In today's information explosion, there is more free content online than ever before, but very little of it is truly valuable. We spend a huge amount of time searching and gathering material, and often all we end up with is a pile of low-quality posts. Paid courses are different: the author has a responsibility to explain the content clearly, and learners, having paid, take it more seriously. Admittedly, paid content is not perfect, but it ensures that the sources of high-quality knowledge receive the reward they deserve, which is vital for the development of the whole industry. First speaker for the negative: Thank you, Chair. Our opponents talk about payment as if it were a master key, and we cannot agree. First, spending money is not the same as learning something. Many people buy courses only for a virtual sense of satisfaction that "I'm making progress"; very few actually listen from beginning to end. Second, many platforms deliberately create anxiety, telling people "if you don't learn, you'll be left behind", which forces them to keep paying. In this atmosphere, buying courses has even become a way of showing off, so much so that learning itself gets neglected. We must not underestimate the influence of commercial marketing on public perception. Second speaker for the affirmative: Our opponents say some people buy courses and never listen, but that is the individual's fault, not a problem with paid knowledge itself. If some people buy a gym membership and never go, does that mean gyms are harmful? Second speaker for the negative: We are not against paying; we simply want to remind everyone that, in the final analysis, learning depends on yourself. There is no need to spend money in order to learn—libraries and free open courses can be just as rewarding. Chair: Thank you both for your excellent speeches. We now move on to the open debate.

reading.title: 为什么总有那么多“巧合”？
reading.zh: 你有没有遇到过这样的事：刚想起一个多年不联系的老同学，手机就响了，打来的正是他；或者在国外旅行，竟然在街头碰到了大学时的室友。很多人会觉得这是缘分，甚至认为冥冥之中有某种力量在安排。可不是吗？这种事听起来实在太神奇了。不过，从科学的角度看，这些“巧合”并没有那么神秘。数学上有个著名的“生日问题”：一个班里只要有二十三个人，其中至少两人同一天生日的概率就会超过一半；如果人数达到六十，这个概率几乎接近百分之百。大多数人第一次听到这个结论都会大吃一惊，因为我们习惯从自己出发去想：“别人跟我同一天生日的可能性很小。”但这个问题问的是任意两个人，可能的组合数量远比我们想象的多。日常生活中的巧合也是同样的道理。打个比方，这就好比买彩票：某一个人中大奖的概率虽说极低，但每期有成千上万的人购买，有人中奖几乎是不可避免的。我们一生中会想起无数个人，也会接到无数个电话，两件事偶尔撞在一起，再正常不过了。只不过，那些没有应验的“想起”，我们转身就忘了，而少量应验的却被牢牢记住，于是巧合在我们的记忆中显现得格外频繁。当然，这并不是说生活就因此失去了浪漫。每一次相识，依然是独一无二的。只是下次再遇到“怎么这么巧”的时候，不妨想一想它背后的数学。
reading.en: Have you ever had this happen: you've just thought of an old classmate you haven't been in touch with for years, and your phone rings—and it's him? Or, travelling abroad, you bump into your university roommate in the street? Many people feel this is fate, and some even believe that some unseen force is arranging things. And who can blame them? Such things really do sound amazing. From a scientific point of view, however, these "coincidences" are not so mysterious. There is a famous problem in mathematics called the "birthday problem": in a class of just twenty-three people, the probability that at least two share a birthday is more than one half; with sixty people, the probability is close to one hundred per cent. Most people are astonished when they first hear this, because we are used to thinking from our own point of view: "The chance that someone else has the same birthday as me is very small." But the question is about any two people, and the number of possible pairs is far greater than we imagine. Coincidences in everyday life work in the same way. To use an analogy, it's like buying lottery tickets: although the probability of any one person winning the jackpot is extremely low, tens of thousands of people buy tickets for each draw, so it is almost inevitable that someone wins. In a lifetime we think of countless people and receive countless phone calls; for the two to coincide now and then is perfectly normal. It's just that we forget straight away all the times we thought of someone and nothing happened, while the few times it "came true" stick firmly in our minds, so coincidences seem to appear especially often in our memories. Of course, this doesn't mean life loses its romance. Every time we meet someone, it is still unique. It's just that next time you find yourself thinking "What a coincidence!", you might like to consider the mathematics behind it.

reading.zh: 在江南一座古镇的小河边，有一家开了一百多年的面馆。店门口那块黑底金字的招牌，据说是清朝末年开张时请当地一位秀才写的，至今已经换过三次框，字却一直没变。店里的招牌菜是蒸南瓜和虾仁面。每天天还没亮，老板老周就要去乡下的农户家挑南瓜。他说，南瓜必须是当天摘的，削皮、切块、上锅蒸，每一步都有讲究：蒸久了容易糊，时间短了又不够甜。“很多年轻人觉得我太较真，可这碗面的味道，就是靠这些细节撑起来的。”这些年，古镇发生了很大的变革。随着旅游业的崛起，街上开满了奶茶店和网红餐厅，不少老店要么关掉，要么改头换面。有人劝老周把店装修得时髦一点，再请个明星做代言人，说不定能吸引更多年轻顾客。老周没有理会。他觉得，老店的价值不在于引人注目，而在于让人吃到熟悉的味道。去年，一位从小在镇上长大、后来移居海外的老人专程回来，一进门就点了一碗虾仁面。他吃得很慢，像是要把每一口都咽进记忆里。临走时，他红着眼睛说：“几十年了，还是这个味儿。”老周说，那一刻，他觉得所有的坚守都值了。至此，这家店已经传到了第四代。老周的女儿大学毕业后回到镇上，开始在网上直播做面的整个流程。没想到，黑白相间的老店、热气腾腾的蒸笼，反而成了年轻人眼里最“潮”的风景。
reading.en: By a little river in an ancient town south of the Yangtze, there is a noodle shop that has been open for more than a hundred years. The gold-on-black signboard over its door is said to have been written by a local scholar when the shop opened in the last years of the Qing dynasty; its frame has been replaced three times, but the characters have never changed. The shop's signature dishes are steamed pumpkin and shrimp noodles. Every day before dawn, the owner, Lao Zhou, goes to farms in the countryside to choose pumpkins. He says the pumpkins must be picked that very day, and every step—peeling, cutting into chunks, steaming—has its rules: steam them too long and they burn; too short and they are not sweet enough. "Lots of young people think I'm too fussy, but it's these details that hold up the flavour of this bowl of noodles." In recent years the old town has changed enormously. With the rise of tourism, the streets have filled with bubble-tea shops and trendy restaurants, and many old shops have either closed down or completely reinvented themselves. People advised Lao Zhou to renovate the shop to look more fashionable and get a celebrity to endorse it, which might attract more young customers. Lao Zhou ignored them. He believes that an old shop's value lies not in grabbing attention but in letting people taste a familiar flavour. Last year an old man who had grown up in the town and later emigrated came back specially. As soon as he walked in, he ordered a bowl of shrimp noodles. He ate very slowly, as if he wanted to swallow every mouthful into his memory. As he left, his eyes red, he said, "After all these decades, it still tastes the same." Lao Zhou says that at that moment he felt all his perseverance had been worth it. The shop has now been passed down to the fourth generation. After graduating from university, Lao Zhou's daughter returned to the town and began livestreaming the whole noodle-making process online. Unexpectedly, the black-and-white old shop and the steaming bamboo baskets have become the "coolest" sight of all in young people's eyes.

reading.title: 古诗词里的当下
reading.zh: 在快节奏的当下，古诗词似乎离我们很远。可只要留心就会发现，它们其实时不时就会出现在日常生活中，只是换了一种方式。朋友圈里，有人加班到深夜，配上一句“夜来风雨声，花落知多少”，调侃自己又掉了不少头发；中秋节一个人在外地，有人发一张月亮的照片，只写“举头望明月，低头思故乡”，满腹心事不必多说，看到的人都有同感。毕业季，同学们各奔东西，留言里少不了那句“海内存知己，天涯若比邻”。教师节，学生们把“春蚕到死丝方尽”送给老师，向辛勤付出的前辈致敬。古人写诗，往往是在向天地倾诉自己的悲欢；今天的人借用这些句子，则是在用一种更含蓄、更优雅的方式表达自己。一千多年前的文字，至今仍能准确地说出现代人的感受，这本身就让人难以置信。当然，也有人担心，网上流行的诗句常常被断章取义，甚至被误导性地解读。比如“人生得意须尽欢”，常被人当作及时行乐的理由，却忽略了李白写这首诗时的苦闷与豪情。从这个视角看，真正读懂一首诗，还有待我们回到原文，从头了解它的背景。总的来说，古诗词并没有离开我们。它们像一座取之不尽的宝库，魅力无穷，等着每一个愿意沉浸其中的人去发现。
reading.en: In today's fast-paced world, classical poetry seems far removed from us. Yet if you pay attention, you will find that it pops up in daily life now and then, only in a different form. On social media, someone who has worked overtime until late at night posts the line "Last night came the sound of wind and rain; who knows how many blossoms fell?", joking that they have lost a lot more hair. Alone in another city at the Mid-Autumn Festival, someone posts a photo of the moon with just the words "I raise my head and gaze at the bright moon; I lower it and think of home"; there is no need to say more about the feelings in their heart, and everyone who sees it feels the same. In graduation season, as classmates go their separate ways, the farewell messages never lack the line "A close friend within the four seas makes the ends of the earth feel like next door." On Teachers' Day, students offer their teachers the line "The silkworm spins its silk until it dies", paying tribute to the hard work of their elders. When the ancients wrote poems, they were often pouring out their joys and sorrows to heaven and earth; when people today borrow these lines, they are expressing themselves in a more subtle and elegant way. That words written more than a thousand years ago can still capture the feelings of modern people so precisely is in itself hard to believe. Of course, some people worry that lines popular online are often taken out of context or even interpreted in misleading ways. For example, "When life goes well, enjoy it to the full" is often treated as an excuse to live for the moment, ignoring the frustration and boldness Li Bai felt when he wrote the poem. From this angle, truly understanding a poem still requires us to go back to the original and learn its background from the beginning. On the whole, classical poetry has not left us. It is like an inexhaustible treasure house of endless charm, waiting to be discovered by anyone willing to immerse themselves in it.

grammar.title: Speech openings: 尊敬的…… / 在此，我谨代表……
grammar.pattern: 尊敬的 + audience · 在此，我谨代表 A，向 B 表示 + 感谢 / 欢迎 / 祝贺
grammar.explain: Formal speeches follow fixed openings. 尊敬的 ("respected") addresses the audience; 在此 ("on this occasion") and the humble adverb 谨 ("respectfully") come before the main verb, as in 我谨代表……向……表示衷心的感谢. grammar.title: Notice formulas: 兹定于 · 届时 · 特此通知
grammar.pattern: 兹定于 + date + event。届时 + request。特此通知。
grammar.explain: Official notices use compact formulas. 兹定于 ("it has hereby been arranged that … on") announces the date of an event, 届时 ("when the time comes; at that time") introduces what should happen on the day, and 特此通知 ("notice is hereby given") closes the notice.

grammar.title: Humble and honorific language
grammar.pattern: humble: 有幸 · 荣幸 · 拙见 / honorific: 贵 + N · 光临 · 指教
grammar.explain: Formal Chinese lowers oneself and raises the listener. Speakers say they are 有幸 ("fortunate enough") or 荣幸 ("honoured") to be present and call their own ideas 拙见 ("my humble opinion"); they refer to the other side with 贵 (贵公司, 贵校) and use verbs such as 光临 ("to honour with one's presence") and 指教 ("to give guidance").

reading.title: 在新生开学典礼上的致辞
reading.zh: 亲爱的同学们，尊敬的各位老师、各位家长：大家上午好！今天，我们欢聚在这里，迎接来自全国各地的三千多名新同学。在此，我谨代表学校，向各位同学表示热烈的欢迎，向一路相伴、无私付出的家长们表示衷心的感谢！我有幸在这所大学工作了三十年，至今还记得自己初次走进校园时的情景：拎着一只旧箱子，在校园里转悠了大半天，才找到寝室。那时的我胆子很小，见到老师都不敢开口说话。是老师们的细心指导、同学们的坦诚相待，帮我渡过了最初那段迷茫的日子。大学的历程，注定不会一帆风顺。你们会遇到考试的压力，也许会经历失恋的痛苦，甚至会怀疑自己。但请记住，每一位成功者的背后，都有成千上万个不为人知的艰辛时刻。所谓成功的秘诀，往往并不神秘，它源于日复一日的坚持。我想重申一点：大学不只是学知识的地方。希望你们积极参加社团活动，多去野外走走，多和不同的人交流，用自己的眼睛看世界。当你们攀上一座又一座山顶，再回头看的时候，就会发现，正是这些经历，填补了书本无法给予的空白。四年后，我们将在这个会场再次相聚。届时，希望每一位同学都能带着收获和自信，潇洒地走向更广阔的天地。谢谢大家！
reading.en: Dear students, respected teachers and parents: Good morning, everyone! Today we are gathered here to welcome more than three thousand new students from all over the country. On behalf of the university, I would like to extend a warm welcome to all of you, and my heartfelt thanks to the parents who have been with you every step of the way and given so selflessly. I have had the good fortune to work at this university for thirty years, and I still remember the first time I walked onto this campus: carrying an old suitcase, I wandered around for the best part of a day before I found my dormitory. I was very timid back then and didn't even dare to speak when I saw a teacher. It was my teachers' careful guidance and my classmates' honesty and openness that helped me through those first confused days. Your journey through university is bound not to be all plain sailing. You will face the pressure of exams, you may go through the pain of heartbreak, and you may even doubt yourselves. But remember: behind every successful person there are thousands of hard moments that no one else sees. The so-called secret of success is usually nothing mysterious; it comes from persevering day after day. I would like to stress one point once more: university is not only a place for acquiring knowledge. I hope you will take an active part in clubs and societies, get out into the countryside, talk with all kinds of people, and see the world with your own eyes. When you have climbed one summit after another and look back, you will find that it is precisely these experiences that have filled the gaps books can never fill. Four years from now, we will meet again in this hall. When that day comes, I hope every one of you will stride out confidently into a wider world, carrying your achievements and your self-belief with you. Thank you all!

chengyu.lit: throw out a brick to attract jade
chengyu.en: to offer modest views to draw out better ones

example.zh: 我先说几句，算是抛砖引玉，希望大家多提意见。
example.en: Let me say a few words first to get the ball rolling—I hope everyone will share their views.

chengyu.lit: many people gathered in one hall

example.zh: 今天各界嘉宾济济一堂，共同庆祝学校成立一百周年。
example.en: Today distinguished guests from all walks of life have gathered to celebrate the school's centenary.

chengyu.lit: everyone plans, everyone contributes
chengyu.en: to pool everyone's wisdom and effort

example.zh: 只要大家群策群力，就没有克服不了的困难。
example.en: As long as we pool our ideas and efforts, there is no difficulty we cannot overcome.

chengyu.lit: words return to the main story
chengyu.en: to get back to the subject

example.zh: 好了，闲话少说，言归正传。
example.en: Right, enough chit-chat—let's get back to the point.

chengyu.lit: make long words short
chengyu.en: to make a long story short

example.zh: 时间有限，我就长话短说。
example.en: Time is limited, so I'll keep it brief.

chengyu.lit: guests arrive as if returning home

example.zh: 这家酒店服务周到，让人有宾至如归的感觉。
example.en: The service at this hotel is so attentive that guests feel right at home.

chengyu.lit: open the door and see the mountain
chengyu.en: to come straight to the point

example.zh: 他开门见山地说明了来意。
example.en: He came straight to the point and explained why he had come.

chengyu.lit: honoured friends fill every seat
chengyu.en: a full house of distinguished guests

example.zh: 开业当天，店里高朋满座，热闹非凡。
